T: Fire meets water. Dinner meets you.
D: A fiery young woman and a soft-hearted water guy fall for each other in Element City.
P: Serve the snacks when Ember works the counter at her family's shop.
S: the spicy snacks sold at the Fireplace shop
Cashews and peanuts tossed with chilli flakes, smoked paprika and honey, roasted at 170C for 12 minutes until glossy and hot.

Flatbreads brushed with harissa stirred into olive oil, grilled until charred at the edges, torn and served with thick labneh. Mix 300g self-raising flour with 300g Greek yoghurt and a pinch of salt into a soft dough and knead 1 minute. Divide into 4 and roll each into a thin oval. Stir 2 tbsp harissa into 3 tbsp olive oil. Cook the flatbreads on a very hot dry pan or grill for 2 minutes a side until puffed and charred at the edges, brushing with the harissa oil as they come off. Spread 250g labneh on a plate, drizzle with oil and za'atar and serve with the torn flatbreads.
Thick cucumber rounds topped with feta whipped with Greek yoghurt and lemon, finished with dill and cracked pepper.
M: Ember's dad Bernie and the shop he built
Lamb shoulder browned, braised with harissa, tomato, chickpeas and cumin at 160C for 3 hours until it pulls apart, with warm flatbread.
dinner with Wade's family in their high-rise

Salmon gently poached in a light broth of ginger, soy and spring onion for 8 minutes, with steamed rice and bok choy. Bring 1L chicken stock to a gentle simmer with 6 slices ginger, 3 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp mirin and 3 spring onions cut into lengths. Lower in 4 skinless salmon fillets and poach gently, never boiling, for 8 minutes. Steam 1.5 cups jasmine rice. Add 4 halved baby bok choy to the broth for the last 2 minutes. Serve the salmon over rice with the bok choy, a ladle of broth, a few drops of sesame oil and thin sliced spring onion.
W: the Vivisteria flower Ember always wanted to see
Meringue baked at 120C for 90 minutes and cooled in the oven, topped with whipped cream, blueberries and edible purple flowers.
K: Apple juice warmed with cinnamon, cloves, orange peel and ginger, served steaming in mugs.

s.note: the spicy snacks sold at the Fireplace shop
s.how: Toss 200g cashews and 200g peanuts with 2 tbsp honey, a pinch of chilli flakes and smoked paprika. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes until glossy. Cool until crunchy and serve hot to the touch in flavour only.

Slice 2 Lebanese cucumbers into thick rounds. Whip 150g feta with 150g Greek yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon until smooth. Pipe or spoon onto each round and finish with dill and cracked pepper. Cool and refreshing, a little teary.

m.note: Ember's dad Bernie and the shop he built
m.how: Brown 1kg diced lamb shoulder, then stir in 2 tbsp harissa and a teaspoon of cumin. Add a can of crushed tomatoes, a can of drained chickpeas and water to cover. Braise at 160C for 3 hours until it pulls apart. Serve with warm flatbread.

w.note: the Vivisteria flower Ember always wanted to see
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Shape into a round and bake at 120C for 90 minutes, then cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream, blueberries and edible purple flowers.

d.how: Heat 1L apple juice with 2 cinnamon sticks, 4 cloves, 3 strips orange peel and 2 slices ginger until steaming, then keep warm for 10 minutes. Strain into mugs and serve with a cinnamon stick in each.
